clue.text: Hear someone sleeping off their guard

parts.note: to catch something is to hear it, as in catching a remark
one means someone, as in 'one never knows'
napping means sleeping, taking a nap

explanation.surface: Somebody overhears a person dozing who has let their guard drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught unawares is to be surprised while unprepared, so the phrase describes someone off their guard.

clue.text: Fall apart when doctor lances troublesome ulcer

indicators.note: a doctor lances an ulcer by piercing it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
troublesome suggests the letters of the next word are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Something gives way as a physician pierces a painful sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' rearranges ULCER into CRULE, and 'lances' puts MB inside it after CRU.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumble is to break into small pieces and disintegrate, a synonym for coming to pieces.

clue.text: Kind prepared is ready for printing

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
set means prepared, as in 'all set'

explanation.surface: A sort that has been got ready is fit for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Typeset text has been arranged in type, so it is composed and prepared for the press.

clue.text: Basil and kit long for a poisonous berry

parts.note: basil is a herb
Kit is a short form of a man's name; written out long it is Christopher

explanation.surface: Two men, Basil and Kit, seem to be pining for a toxic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil and Kit look like names in the surface; Basil is the plant and Kit the pet form of a longer name, which 'long' asks for in full.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant is the baneberry, whose shiny berries are toxic.

clue.text: Element, a short story of the newly-born

parts.note: neon is a chemical element

indicators.note: short means the following word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chemical element and a brief story concern newborn babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal is the medical adjective for the first weeks of a baby's life.

clue.text: Observe warning

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch out for a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to spot or note something; a warning is advance notification, as in 'two weeks' notice'.

clue.text: General goes to proprietor's joint, it is not in private hands

definitions.text: it is not in private hands

parts.note: public means general, belonging to everyone
an owner is a proprietor; the possessive gives the S
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A military officer visits the landlord's pub, which is no privately held business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank and 'joint' like a bar; they are an adjective and a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: State ownership means the community or government holds the asset rather than individuals.

clue.text: One new grassy area near the wicket

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a field is a grassy area

explanation.surface: A fresh patch of turf by the stumps on a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the set of stumps at the centre of the ground; fielders placed close to it are said to field in this zone.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this word means close to the batsman, the region inside the outfield.

clue.text: One telling jokes shuts up better half

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: half asks for one half of the next word, here its second three letters

explanation.surface: A comedian silences their spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse; 'half' takes TER, the back half of BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a comedian or joker who tells gags.

clue.text: More important to have the majority at the top

parts.note: upper means higher in rank, more important
most means the majority

explanation.surface: The bigger share counts for more when it sits highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest in position, the summit of something.

clue.text: Ask field officer inside to make it less visible

indicators.note: inside places the officer's letters within the word for ask

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly

explanation.surface: Someone asks an army officer in to blur the view.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to cloud or obscure, as fog hides a view.

clue.text: Primary scholar, individual entering signal corps

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

indicators.note: entering puts the letter for individual into the corps abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for signal corps
I as a single individual, the first person

explanation.surface: A star pupil enlists in the army's communications unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental or elementary, synonyms of primary.

clue.text: Person with constructive ideas

parts.note: constructive seems to mean helpful, but here it is literal: ideas about building, those of a designer of buildings

explanation.definitionFit: This professional designs buildings, so their ideas are literally about construction.

clue.text: Always including wrong mark on the outside

indicators.note: including means the word for always holds the mark inside it

parts.note: eternal means lasting always
X is the cross a teacher marks against a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher forever puts a cross against errors in the margin.
explanation.definitionFit: External means outer or exterior, located outside.

clue.text: We drop various fine particles

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: We let fall assorted tiny bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the six letters of WE DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Powder is a mass of tiny dry grains, such as dust or flour.

clue.text: Give previous 5 of warren disintegrating

indicators.note: disintegrating means the words fall apart and their letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Earlier warning that a rabbit warren is crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' is the answer to 5 down, NOTICE, so the definition reads 'give previous notice'. 'disintegrating' rearranges OF WARREN.
explanation.definitionFit: To forewarn is to alert someone in advance, giving them early notification.

clue.text: Carriage holding a pound in coins

indicators.note: holding means the word for coins contains the other letters

parts.note: cash is money in coins
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A vehicle containing a pound sterling in loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: A calash is a light horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Greek character not in favour of wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, not in favour of

explanation.surface: A Greek man opposed to drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Lottie's upset by the understatement

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the name are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive S supplies seven letters

explanation.surface: A girl called Lottie is offended by someone's understatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LOTTIES, using the S of the possessive too.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that understates by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad'.

clue.text: I leave mysterious indicator of violent storms

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the remaining letters are jumbled into an obscure order
I leave tells the solver to remove the letter I from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster quits, having found a puzzling sign of severe gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' takes one I out of INDICATOR, leaving NDICATOR, which 'mysterious' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tornadic is the adjective for whirlwinds, the twisters of a severe storm.

clue.text: Philanderer coming from anjou during extremes of depression

indicators.note: during means one part sits in the middle of the other
extremes of picks the first and last letters of the next word
coming from suggests the letters of the place name are made into something new

explanation.surface: A womaniser from the Anjou region of France arrives in a gloomy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' gives D and N from DEPRESSION; 'coming from' rearranges ANJOU into ONJUA; 'during' places that between D and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Spanish seducer's name has become a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Hide at one time in western state

indicators.note: in means the words for at one time go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is a short form for California, a state in the western US
once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: Someone once went into hiding in California.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal is to keep something out of sight, a synonym of hide.

clue.text: Sort of status that's odd, having minimum number for meeting

parts.note: the status quo is a sort of status, so this word follows status in that phrase
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange kind of standing gives the smallest attendance a committee needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of status' points to the Latin phrase status quo, the existing state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the least count of members who must be present for a meeting's decisions to be valid.

clue.text: Make known something strange

parts.note: to bring forward something unfamiliar to people, presenting what was new so that it becomes familiar

explanation.definitionFit: To introduce is to present or bring in something new, making it familiar to others.

clue.text: Arrest coming from car uninjured

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A driver walks away unhurt from a crash and is detained by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is informal for an arrest by police.

clue.text: Nick isn't chief

parts.note: isn't is a negative, giving not

explanation.surface: Nick is not the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick and a notch are both small cuts made in an edge.

clue.text: By the way it's an inn

definitions.text: By the way it's an inn

parts.words: By the way it's an inn
parts.note: by the way looks like an aside but is literal: a hostelry sited beside the highway

explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is a pub or inn on a main road outside a town, serving travellers.

clue.text: Document placed in front of board in car

indicators.note: placed in front of means the first word's synonym comes before the second's

parts.note: an instrument is a formal legal document
a panel is a flat board

explanation.surface: A paper is put ahead of a committee meeting held in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a committee; it is a flat sheet, and 'in car' is where the whole thing is found.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard of a vehicle holding dials and gauges is found in a car.
